main_text.p: pericolorum. Summa totius rei, ut in pace contrahatur, hoc redit. Non si [illegible, ~3 letters] iniuria afficiantur privatae aliquae personae; [illegible, ~12 letters] de quibus enim merito requiri potest, publica quaedam praescriptiones [?] consessum est statim [illegible, ~6 letters] quale aliter effet de hac pœnali ad remedia adhibenda extraordinaria, quæ sint contra Legem. Quod si sest situs sit merus [illegible, ~4 letters] in statuto [illegible, ~5 letters] si sest crimen [?], nihil aliud fiat, quod Legibus non est præscriptum: Principi ses est, ex Præfatio præscriptio, sed si subditi ses est, ex præscripto Principe sestuntur, (modo nihil sit in ipsis præjudicium) præcipue necessitate in posse-sione, à veris se sententia persuasioni Legem suadere, ut perspicuè Partes subseruntur, equus solus, ut supremæ legi infestantur. Ergo sic si [?] pœnæ sest imperio seu commodè pos[?] quæ reliqua sunt præstant. Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi, &c.

page.notes: The scan is very faint. Most of the lines are unreadable, and I did not read them with confidence, so the text above is a best-effort reading with illegible markers. The upside-down text in the middle of the page is show-through from the reverse side and is not transcribed. The stamp "6 MA 50" and the rule are excluded. The right edge shows a partial strip of the adjacent page (a large initial H and lines beginning "De", "jamq", "pora", "coort", "adve", "poste"), which is cropped and not transcribed. The catchword at lower left is uncertain and may be show-through.
